title: Model the rejection, then retest it cold
statement: Model rejecting a known misconception in the worked example, then retest it cold on a new tempting case, with no hints before the attempt and the repair only in feedback.
detail: An audit's verification pass attacked a Grade 5 lesson's misconception design as a possible leak and upheld it against the live build: the worked example pre-models the rejected hunter-to-prey reading, and the independent trap item is attempt-first, with no hints before the try and the repair only in post-attempt feedback. The course's bar pins the pre-modelling at the worked example and a cold re-elicitation at release. The worked example works the first arrow on the map and the release item asks about the second, so the retest is on a new case.
against: The lesson's design note and its evaluation document describe the design as elicit-only, "The misconception is elicited, never pre-taught" (grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/content/u4l2-content.json, line 519) and "hunter→prey is THE misconception, elicited and repaired only AFTER an attempt." (grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-deploy/EVALUATION-API.md, lines 93-94), which the audit calls a mislabel. The record refute-the-misconception-learners-bring draws the belief out first, as a prediction, before refuting it. The audit shows the design is canonical and not a leak, not that it teaches better.

evidence.quote: Misconception pre-teach design (I-do models, You-do re-elicits cold) is canonical, not a leak.
